subject: english-language
source_note: Topic structure follows the OCR A-Level English Language specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Exploring Language (Component 01)
units.blurb: Close analysis of authentic texts and original writing on a topical language issue

units.name: Dimensions of Linguistic Variation (Component 02)
units.blurb: How children acquire language, language in the media and language change over time

units.name: Independent Language Research (Component 03)
units.blurb: A personal language investigation presented as a report and an academic poster

topics.name: Language Under the Microscope
topics.blurb: Analysing lexis, semantics, grammar, pragmatics and discourse in a short written text

topics.name: Writing About a Topical Language Issue
topics.blurb: Original writing for a real-world purpose, form and audience exploring language attitudes

topics.name: Comparing & Contrasting Texts
topics.blurb: Linguistic connections across modes: spoken vs written, spontaneous vs crafted, dialect varieties

topics.name: Child Language Acquisition
topics.blurb: Children's spoken language 0-7, IPA transcription and acquisition theory

topics.name: Language in the Media
topics.blurb: Multi-modal media texts through language and power, gender and technology

topics.name: Language Change
topics.blurb: Historical varieties of English compared across two texts from different times

topics.name: An Independent Investigation of Language
topics.blurb: A self-chosen investigation: research focus, methodology, data analysis and conclusions

topics.name: The Academic Poster
topics.blurb: A concise, multi-modal poster presenting the investigation for a conference audience

connections.why: Studying authentic texts in Section A models the styles learners emulate when writing about a language issue
The same language-level toolkit drives both single-text analysis and comparison across texts
Engaging with attitudes to varieties and modes feeds both the original writing and the comparison task
The lexis, grammar, pragmatics and discourse framework is reapplied to children's spoken data
Close analysis of features and effects underpins evaluating multi-modal media texts
Comparing two texts and exploring contextual effects is the exact skill used across historical periods
Reading across modes prepares learners to analyse the multi-modal discourse of media texts
Both sections are synoptic, drawing theory and language levels together to interpret real data
Power, gender and technology theories illuminate why and how usage shifts over time
Systematic close analysis of data is the core analytical skill of the independent investigation
Acquisition, media and change supply theories and questions learners pursue independently
Media analysis is a popular springboard for self-chosen investigation topics
Language-change methodology models the data-led approach of the investigation
Critically evaluating attitudes to language is rehearsed before framing an investigation's focus
The poster distils the completed investigation's context, methodology, results and conclusions
Both demand shaping a text creatively for a specific real-world purpose and audience
